failure_mode_prevented: Asking questions answered by the repository
rule: Read conversational context and discover relevant technical facts; clarify vague intent before broad inspection; do not infer user goals from code.

failure_mode_prevented: Premature decomposition or an exhausting questionnaire
rule: Ask the highest-impact unresolved question or small related group; follow up on answers; skip settled subjects; use concrete scenarios to expose ambiguity.

failure_mode_prevented: Question quotas or unnecessary follow-up turns
rule: Ask only when the answer could materially change goal/scope/design/acceptance/next iteration; otherwise state a reversible assumption or defer the detail.

failure_mode_prevented: Endless interviewing or a plan built on hidden assumptions
rule: Synthesize outcome/scope/approach/constraints/success evidence; proceed when material decisions are clear and remaining uncertainty is bounded; no ritual approval turn.

failure_mode_prevented: Turning unresolved user intent into a research ticket
rule: Resolve consequential intent conversationally; use bounded investigation for empirical unknowns; keep proposed defaults distinct from user decisions.

failure_mode_prevented: Continuing to interrogate after the user asks for a draft
rule: Honor a request to stop questions with a provisional plan and explicit assumptions; do not claim unresolved choices were agreed.

failure_mode_prevented: Duplicating existing work or assuming integration works
rule: Give requirements stable IDs and covered/partial/missing/unverified status with evidence.

failure_mode_prevented: Overlooking lifecycle and consumer behavior
rule: Map actors; transitions; external boundaries; failure/recovery paths; final observable outcome.

failure_mode_prevented: Incompatible slices or invented implementation details
rule: Specify cross-slice inputs/outputs and invariants; distinguish observed facts from proposed design.

failure_mode_prevented: Freezing a design before empirical uncertainty is resolved
rule: Give research a question; investigation limit; evidence; decision rule; affected follow-up slices.

failure_mode_prevented: Ticket lists replacing project planning
rule: Plan coherent capability or learning increments before issue bodies; an iteration can contain several vertical issues.

failure_mode_prevented: Executing a fixed backlog despite new evidence
rule: Give each iteration evidence and a next-step rule; revise later iterations after review; use ordinary acceptance for predictable work.

failure_mode_prevented: Overdesigning future work or losing final scope
rule: Detail the next iteration; account for remaining scope with conditional outcomes and prerequisites; do not freeze decisions that depend on earlier results.

failure_mode_prevented: Layer tickets that deliver no usable behavior
rule: Slice by consumer scenario through every needed layer; include wiring and verification.

failure_mode_prevented: Large foundations delaying useful evidence
rule: First delivery slice proves a narrow real input-to-consumer path with minimal necessary setup.

failure_mode_prevented: Deferring essential protections to hardening
rule: Include authorization and retry/concurrency correctness when the exposed behavior needs them.

failure_mode_prevented: Oversized tickets or fragmented implementation layers
rule: Split independent behaviors; merge fragments that cannot be demonstrated separately; use uncertainty and reviewability.

failure_mode_prevented: Automatic schema/config/foundation tickets
rule: Separate enablement only for a concrete boundary; name immediate consumer and independently verifiable exit condition.

failure_mode_prevented: Workers missing decisions from conversation
rule: Embed relevant requirements and exact shared contracts; link broader context without copying the entire plan.

failure_mode_prevented: Invented commands or smoke proof presented as full proof
rule: State actual command/procedure and expected evidence; mark unknown commands and unavailable environments.

failure_mode_prevented: Unlimited HITL tasks and unnecessary approval rituals
rule: Name the human decision and evidence; permit independent work within existing authorization.

failure_mode_prevented: Unnecessary chains or hidden prerequisites
rule: Each hard dependency names the artifact/capability/decision and release condition it provides.

failure_mode_prevented: File layout dictating product issue boundaries
rule: Track shared edits and resource constraints separately from hard dependencies; coordinate execution.

failure_mode_prevented: Shared requirements and invariants lost between issues
rule: Map every requirement to delivery owners and a final proof owner; repeat relevant invariants in affected slices.

failure_mode_prevented: Intermediate tickets produce no usable capability
rule: Demonstrate each delivery slice after its prerequisites; justify supporting exceptions.

failure_mode_prevented: Duplicate or unnecessary issues
rule: Remove each issue mentally and explain what required outcome would be lost.

failure_mode_prevented: Hidden final wiring or operational work
rule: Assign consumer wiring and final composition proof; preserve tests inside each slice.

failure_mode_prevented: Conditional later work silently disappears
rule: Account for all requested requirements; keep decision-dependent slices provisional with explicit gates.

failure_mode_prevented: User corrections leave stale plans or dependency graphs
rule: Update affected design decisions; iterations; contracts; coverage; bodies; and dependencies together while preserving stable IDs.

failure_mode_prevented: Creating documents and a full backlog for every planning conversation
rule: Deliver shared understanding and iteration map first; create durable files and detailed issues only to the depth requested.

failure_mode_prevented: Duplicate issues or incorrect tracker dependencies
rule: Prepare bodies; publish only when authorized; use returned IDs; read back links; reconcile partial failures before retrying.

failure_mode_prevented: Closed issues treated as proof of readiness
rule: Recheck actual artifact and integration state before execution; issue closure alone is insufficient.
